extraction.name: COMMONSENSE QA
extraction.description: A challenging new dataset for commonsense question answering. To capture common sense beyond associations, we extract from CONCEPTNET multiple target concepts that have the same semantic relation to a single source concept. Crowd-workers are asked to author multiple-choice questions that mention the source concept and discriminate in turn between each of the target concepts.
extraction.creator: Alon Talmor, Jonathan Herzig, Nicholas Lourie, Jonathan Berant
extraction.publisher: Tel-Aviv University, Allen Institute for Artificial Intelligence
extraction.citeAs: Talmor, A., Herzig, J., Lourie, N., & Berant, J. (2019). COMMONSENSE QA: A Question Answering Challenge Targeting Commonsense Knowledge. arXiv:1811.00937v2.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: We extract from CONCEPTNET multiple target concepts that have the same semantic relation to a single source concept. Crowd-workers are asked to author multiple-choice questions that mention the source concept and discriminate in turn between each of the target concepts. Workers add distractors and verify quality.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Filter triplets with general relations (e.g., RelatedTo) or relations that are already well-explored in NLP (e.g., IsA). Filter triplets where one of the concepts is more than four words or not in English. Filter triplets where the edit distance between c1 and c2 is too low.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: AMT workers saw the question concept and three answer concepts. They were asked to formulate three questions, where all questions contain the question concept. Each question should have as an answer one of the answer concepts, but not the other two. Workers added one distractor from CONCEPTNET and one manual distractor. A disjoint group of workers verified the generated questions.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Each question is verified by 2 workers, and only questions verified by at least one worker that answered correctly are used. This processes filters out 15% of the questions.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: 122 formulators contributed to question generation. However, 10 workers formulated more than 85% of the questions.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: 10 workers formulated more than 85% of the questions.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The best baseline (BERT-large) obtains 56% accuracy, well below human performance (89%). Questions often require background knowledge that is seldom explicitly reported on the web due to reporting bias.
